thread:
maria: Quick proposal — thinking we should move a lightweight RBAC prefilter into the console query gateway to avoid paying auth checks on the slow-path. This is to cut p50/p95 token latency for dashboard panel queries that fan out a lot.

ashok: Can you sketch the tradeoffs? sounds like more logic in the gateway vs more filtering later.

maria: Exactly. Pros: early rejection means we never allocate KV/cache or remote shard work for denied requests; reduces tail work. Cons: gateway becomes heavier and needs access to up-to-date perms (more sync/invalidations), potential for stale denies if we cache too long.

samir: Do we have numbers that show how much work is saved?

maria: Quick microbench from dev cluster: panel query with 10 fanout shards, baseline p95 = 410ms, after prefilter reject (simulated 30% rejects) p95 drops to ~290ms. Overall CPU down ~18% on query plane. (these are synthetic)

jen: What about mixed auth cases where perms are attribute-based and require enrichment? Can't do that at the gateway.

maria: Right — gateway only handles cheap checks: token scopes, capability buckets, tenant mappings. For attribute-based or resource-rich checks we fall back to control plane enrichment (slow path).

lee: How do we keep gateway perms fresh without querying control plane for every request? That was my main worry.

maria: Plan: push updates from control plane as deltas over a small pubsub channel and keep a short TTL local cache. For corner cases we allow a short-circuit validation call to control plane when cache miss or ambiguity. Also expose a debug endpoint to invalidate keys per-tenant.

ashok: Sounds promising. Would we still need the current post-filter step? I assume yes for fine-grained checks.

maria: Yes — design is layered: 1) gateway prefilter (fast rejects/allow), 2) query executor does full check post-materialization when needed. Prefilter is only an optimization for the common-path checks.

jen: I want a fallback policy for when the delta sync lags (eg. during control plane deploy). We shouldn't accidentally allow a request.

maria: Agreed. Default on ambiguous or stale entry -> conservative deny. Also add a permissive-mode flag for canary tenants.

samir: What about batching? We talked about tenant-weighted batching for GPU serving but here we can do request multiplexing in the gateway to reduce backend SLO pressure. Any sketch?

maria: Gateway will expose a configurable `batch_window_ms` (default 6ms) and tenant-weight parameter to avoid starving low-volume tenants. Example config: \n\n```\ngateway.auth_prefilter:\n  enabled: true\n  cache_ttl_ms: 750\n  batch_window_ms: 6\n  tenant_weight_policy: proportional\n```\n
lee: 6ms seems tiny but it helps pool micro-requests. We must measure added latency.

ops-bot: deploy status: last gateway deploy 5032109000 succeeded in staging. Canary flagged for auth-prefilter feature gate.

ashok: Also need to think about observability — we should emit metrics: prefilter_evaluations, prefilter_misses, prefilter_denies, sync_lag_seconds.

maria: Yep — and a new dashboard panel with heatmap of prefilter reject rate vs backend latency. If reject rate spikes we know something changed in permissions.

jen: What about RBAC complexity growth? If we keep adding rules into the gateway eventually it becomes the single source of complexity. Maybe we keep the gateway rules deliberately small: only token->tenant mapping, scope allowlist, rate-bucket checks. Everything else stays downstream.

maria: That's the plan — minimal capability checks only. We should add a linting step on control plane rules to mark rules as `gateway_eligible` during rule authoring.

samir: Migration path? How do we cut over without big risk?

maria: Feature-gated rollout: 1) start with read-only dashboards, 2) enable prefilter for a small set of low-risk tenants (canary), 3) compare metrics and tail latencies, 4) incrementally expand. Include a global kill-switch.

lee: Do we need a perf test harness that simulates fanout and rejects? We should add to the perf lab.

maria: I'll add a perf scenario to the dashboard load tests and attach the script in the RFC follow-up.

ashok: One misc thought — we might leverage the existing access-token cache used by console to avoid duplicating logic. That reduces work.

maria: Good call. I'll prototype by reusing token cache and instrumenting the delta sync path.

jen: threading question — will this change impact how we do A/B panel rendering? If some panels go through prefilter and some not, we might get inconsistent behavior.

maria: We'll keep consistent by defaulting panel-level config to inherit tenant prefilter behavior. Only explicit opt-in at panel route to bypass.

samir: Ok. Can you write the RFC follow-up with config, metrics, and rollout checklist? I'll help with perf tests.

maria: Will do — drafting now, will ping y'all for review. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: please add the feature flag to the feature-flags spreadsheet before canary.
